A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CD-MoE and provide readable main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and movement between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original compression and fine-tuning results, expert and layer selection ablations, timing measurements, and calibration-data experiments. Appendix A.4 includes original Qwen1.5-MoE results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds larger-model, mathematical reasoning, code generation, layer-output deviation, and audio-derived calibration experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains greedy expert and layer selection using JS divergence, calibration-averaged fixed gates, shared experts, and fine-tuning restricted to condensed layers. Algorithms 1–2 remain equivalent. Expanded explanations of K, N, and the S/SR variants clarify configurations already represented in v2.

E1.justification: v3 adds GSM8K mathematical reasoning and HumanEval code generation evaluations in Table 4, extending beyond the original eight benchmarks. Appendix A.2 adds an Emilia audio-derived calibration scenario. The original C4, downstream calibration, commonsense, MMLU, and fine-tuning datasets remain; Qwen1.5 results were already present in v2.

E2.justification: v3 adds expert-merging comparisons labeled M-SMoE in Table 1 and MC-SMoE in Tables 2–4, without clarifying that distinction. It also adds LayerDrop to the fine-tuned comparison. The GPT-Neo, OPT, BLOOM, and OpenLLaMA reference rows from v2 Table 7 are omitted from the corresponding Qwen1.5 table. LayerTrim/BlockTrim becoming LayerDrop/BlockDrop is a renaming.

E3.justification: Added experimental settings include the 57B Qwen2-MoE model evaluated on six retained benchmarks, accuracy evaluation on GSM8K, and Pass@1 evaluation on HumanEval. Section 4.3 introduces a fine-tuned LayerDrop control that updates self-attention sublayers. The original 100-example C4 calibration setting and proposed method's fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Two focused analyses are added: Figure 5 compares layer-output distortion for BlockDrop, CD-MoE-S, and CD-MoE-SR, while Appendix A.2 tests sensitivity to audio-derived calibration. Existing expert-selection, layer-selection, and search-metric ablations remain. The earlier appendix's KL and perplexity analysis is incorporated into Figure 2 rather than removed.

E5.justification: v2 provides single-run SFT point estimates and states that all experiments used one run. v3 Table 1 introduces means and standard deviations over three random seeds for the central SFT comparisons. It also first specifies 5,000 inference repetitions for latency measurement. However, Appendix A.1 retains the contradictory statement that all experiments used a single run.

E6.justification: v3 adds larger-model, math/code, merging-baseline, fine-tuned LayerDrop, audio-calibration, and output-distortion results. For example, Table 3 reports 70.5 average accuracy for both CD-MoE variants versus 71.8 unpruned across six tasks. Table 1 replaces the earlier CD-MoE-SR SFT point estimate of 60.5 with a reported three-seed summary of 60.4 ± 0.2; this is not evidence of a same-estimator performance decline. Retained zero-shot and search-ablation table values match.

T1.justification: New Section 3.4 supplies computational-complexity reasoning: O(K·E) for greedy expert selection and O(N·L) for greedy layer selection, contrasted with exhaustive search. v2 reported inference counts and timing but lacked these asymptotic arguments. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain condensation of shared-expert MoEs, efficient greedy selection, and lightweight recovery through fine-tuning. The abstract and introduction retain the headline 27.5% memory reduction, 1.26× speedup, approximately 90% accuracy retention, and 98% recovery claims. Additional supporting experiments and generalized conclusion wording do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting shared-expert retention to lower output distortion and better recovery than fine-tuned LayerDrop. It interprets the audio-calibration results as evidence of limited calibration-dataset dependence. The dedicated Limitations and Potential Risk sections are removed, including qualifications about architectures without shared experts and selection-related bias; the shared-expert applicability boundary remains elsewhere.

D1.justification: v3 documents fixed-input latency and peak-memory measurement procedures, adds Qwen2 parameter/expert configurations in Table A.1, and identifies wav2vec processing for Emilia calibration. It drops the explicit Block Influence description of the trimming baselines. The existing bf16 precision, A100 hardware, learning rate, warm-up, scheduler, and code availability remain materially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning against expert merging through Li et al.'s Merge, then Compress work, alongside citations supporting GSM8K, HumanEval, Emilia, wav2vec, and OWL. The ShortGPT/Block Influence attribution is removed. The Related Work section's broader positioning remains largely unchanged; consolidating duplicate Mixtral references is bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: Most introduction, related-work, method, and analysis prose is retained. Local revisions clarify variant definitions, metrics, and ranking procedures. Appendix analyses are integrated into the main text, the dedicated limitations/risk sections disappear, and author information and acknowledgements change. These are limited narrative revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one column throughout. Figures 3–4 change from horizontal strips to two-row grids; the old KL/PPL plots merge into Figure 2. The Qwen1.5 table moves into the main text, SFT tables gain uncertainty rows, new evaluation tables and Figure 5 appear, and the calibration plot becomes Table A.2 with an audio row.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's unfine-tuned trimming baselines and single-run SFT evidence, v3 adds an expert-merging comparison, a fine-tuned LayerDrop control, and reported SFT variability. Math/code and larger-model tests also broaden empirical support. These improve assessability, but contradictory run statements, unclear M-SMoE/MC-SMoE naming, and removal of the explicit limitations discussion temper the overall gain.
